spans.text: The following is said in the house of an Avel during the week of Shivah, on days on which Tachanun is not said:
The focus of this chapter is that if we put our trust in Hashem He will protect us, and that despite all our difficulties, all that He does is for our best.

—מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד שָׁמְרֵנִי Please, Hashem, protect me, for I put all my faith in You! —שִׁוִּיתִי יְהֹוָה לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד I constantly look directly to Hashem (for guidance and protection); —כִּי מִימִינִי בַּל אֶמּוֹט He is constantly at my side. Therefore, I am happy and secure, because I know that You will never abandon me!

—קַוֵּה אֶל יְהֹוָה Put your trust in Hashem; (and) —חֲזַק וְיַאֲמֵץ לְבֶּךָ that itself will give you the courage and strength to persevere! (And if Hashem has not yet given you what you asked for); —וְקַוֵּה אֶל יְהֹוָה continue to place your trust in Hashem (for there is no other power to rely on but Hashem alone)!

—אֵין כֵּאלֹהֵינוּ There is no other power like Hashem our King! Therefore, we thank You, for You are the Source of all blessing and salvation. And it was to You alone that (in the times of the Beis Hamikdash) we offered the Ketores.
A section from Maseches Kerisos describing in detail the exact ingredients of the Ketores, how the Ketores was made, and what invalidated the Ketores.
In the beis medrash of Eliyahu it was taught: Anyone who studies halachah every day is assured a place in Olam Haba!

Said Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Chanina: Talmidei chachamim increase peace in the world. Those who love Torah will have peace (will not fear from their enemies), and the yetzer hara will not place stumbling blocks in their path. May there be peace (from wars) in Yerushalayim, serenity, and calm within its inhabitants. May the Beis Hamikdash be rebuilt, and may Hashem give all of Bnei Yisrael strength (to conquer our spiritual and physical enemies) and grant us all (inner and outer) peace!

—יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא (The person saying Kaddish proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.

אָמֵן. יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא—(We all enthusiastically respond:) Absolutely correct! May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise!

—יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח (The person saying Kaddish then points out that) in reality, the true greatness and power of Hashem far exceeds any praises that we mere humans could say. And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely correct!

—עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל רַבָּנַן (The person saying Kaddish requests:) May there be abundant peace, mercy, kindness, long life, and material abundance—from our Father in Heaven—upon all of Bnei Yisrael, and specifically upon our teachers, their students, and all who study Torah—here and everywhere! And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely, we agree!

יְהֵא שְׁלָמָא רַבָּא—(The person saying Kaddish requests:) May there be abundant peace, that comes from Heaven, and life, upon us and upon all of Bnei Yisrael! And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely, we agree!

עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו—(The person saying Kaddish requests:) May He Who makes peace in the Heavens bring about peace upon us and upon all of Bnei Yisrael! And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely, we agree!
In Israel, the following is added:
In Israel, on days when the Torah is not read, some have the custom of saying Barchu.
